## Upload an XML file which does not meet the Crossref schema
Setup: You must be logged in using a pure publisher account (no other privileges)

Go to the "Upload Article XML" tab in the "Publisher Area"

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//publisher/uploadfile

Browse for a file under "Select a file" and select a file from your computer which is XML but not of the Crossref schema. You may use the file "schema_invalid.xml" from the Crossref folder in resources for this test.

Test Resource: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DOAJ/doaj/feature/2861_abstract_rich_text/doajtest/xml_upload_test_package/Crossref/schema_invalid.xml
Choose "Crossref 5.3.1 XML" from "Format of the file" dropdown
Click "Upload"

Expected Test Results: A flash message appears at the top of the screen indicating an error has occurred

Your file is shown in the "History of uploads" with status "processing failed" and a suitable entry in the "Notes" (you may need to reload the page). Check that the explanation link goes to a suitable reason and resolution for the problem.

Action: ## Successfully upload a file containing rich text (JATS) formatting in the title and abstract

Setup: Use the publisher_with_journal testdrive to setup for this test at /testdrive/publisher_with_journal. Keep the testdrive tab open and do the test in a separate tab, as leaving the testdrive page tears it down
Setup: The testdrive creates a journal with ISSNs "1111-1111" and "2222-2222", so make sure no other journal on the system has these ISSNs, otherwise the upload will fail
Setup: You will also need an administrator account for the final step
Setup: At the end of the test please use the 'teardown' link provided by the testdrive to remove test assets (including the uploaded article) from the system
Log in as the publisher account specified by the testdrive result

Go to the "Upload Article XML" tab in the "Publisher Area"

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//publisher/uploadfile

Browse for a file under "Select a file" and select the test resource file "jats_rich_text.xml" from the Crossref 5.3.1 resources

Test Resource: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DOAJ/doaj/feature/2861_abstract_rich_text/doajtest/xml_upload_test_package/Crossref/5.3.1/jats_rich_text.xml
Choose "Crossref 5.3.1 XML" from "Format of the file" dropdown
Click "Upload"

Expected Test Results: A flash message appears at the top of the screen indicating a successful upload
Your file is shown in the "History of uploads" with status "pending"

Action: wait a short amount of time for the job to process, then reload the page (do not re-submit the form data). If the job remains in "pending", reload the page until the status changes.

Expected Test Results: Your file is shown in the "History of uploads" with status "successfully processed", and the Note "1 articles imported (1 new, 0 updated)"

Action:
Go to the Table of Contents for the journal (e.g. by going to /toc/2222-2222), and go to the Articles tab

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//toc/2222-2222

Expected Test Results: The list of articles contains an article titled "Rich text TiOx/Pt3Ti(111) and E=mc2", where the "x" is an italic subscript, the "3" is a subscript and the "2" is a superscript
No literal tags such as "<sub>", "<i>" or "<sub>" are visible in the title

Action: Click "Abstract" on that article to expand it

Expected Test Results: The abstract reads "Films grown on a Pt3Ti(111) surface. Phases z-TiOx and w-TiOx were produced. Energy scales as c2. Second paragraph with <script>alert('xss')</script> text."
The "3" in "Pt3Ti" is a subscript, each "x" in "TiOx" is an italic subscript, the word "produced" is bold, and the "2" in "c2" is a superscript
No text from the abstract is missing (in particular "Ti(111) surface", which follows the first subscript, is present)
The text "<script>alert('xss')</script>" is shown literally as plain text; no alert pop-up appears

Action: Click the article title to open the public article page

Expected Test Results: The page heading shows the title with the same subscript/superscript/italic formatting as on the Table of Contents, with no literal tags visible
The abstract shows the same formatting as on the Table of Contents, and the "<script>alert('xss')</script>" text is shown literally with no alert pop-up
The browser tab title shows the article title as plain text ("Rich text TiOx/Pt3Ti(111) and E=mc2 ...") with no "<sub>", "<i>" or "<sup>" tags in it

Action: View the page source of the article page and find the "citation_title" meta tag

Expected Test Results: The content of the "citation_title" meta tag is "Rich text TiOx/Pt3Ti(111) and E=mc2" with no HTML tags in it

Action:
Go to the public article search and search for "Rich text TiOx"

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//search/articles

Expected Test Results: The article is found and its title and (expanded) abstract are rendered with the same formatting as on the Table of Contents, with no literal tags visible

Action:
Log in as an administrator, go to the "Journals & Articles" search in the admin area and search for "Rich text TiOx"

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//admin/admin_site_search

Expected Test Results: The article's title is shown with the same formatting, with no literal tags visible
Click "(show/hide)" next to the Abstract; the abstract is shown with the same formatting, and "<script>alert('xss')</script>" is shown literally with no alert pop-up
